question: A thick, non-conducting spherical shell with inner radius R and outer radius 2R contains a charge distribution with a non-uniform volume charge density $ρ(r) = A/r$ for $R \le r \le 2R$, where A is a positive constant. A point charge $-Q$ is fixed at the center of the shell. It is observed that the electric field is zero for all points outside the shell ($r > 2R$). Based on this observation, what is the magnitude of the electric field at a radial distance of $r = 3R/2$?
